title: Foliage wind sway material with gusts
purpose: Make grass, crops, reeds and foliage sway in the wind on the GPU: blades bend along the wind more with height (roots stay put), from travelling layered sines plus integer-hash gusts phased by each instance's position, with a root-to-tip colour ramp. Works on InstancedMesh; the wind has an exact CPU mirror.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: three.js r155 or later passed in as THREE (GLSL ES 3.00 uint arithmetic; the fragment stage includes the tonemapping_fragment and colorspace_fragment chunks); only 0.186.1 was run.

contract.language: ECMAScript 2020 module; GLSL ES 3.00 through three.js ShaderMaterial

exports.name: createFoliageWindMaterial
exports.summary: The double-sided foliage material; set uniforms.uTime.value every frame.

exports.name: foliageWindUniforms
exports.summary: The uniform values, to share the wind with another material or a probe.

exports.name: windOffset
exports.signature: windOffset(position, anchor, time, options = {}) -> [x, y, z]
exports.summary: CPU mirror: the world offset of an object-space vertex on a blade standing at a world anchor.

exports.name: windGustNoise
exports.summary: CPU mirror of the gust value noise (integer hash, smoothstep between cells).

exports.name: FOLIAGE_WIND_GLSL
exports.summary: GLSL windHash, windGust and vec3 windOffset(vec3 position, vec3 anchor, float time).

exports.name: FOLIAGE_WIND_VERTEX
exports.summary: Vertex stage with the wind, InstancedMesh aware.

options.name: direction
options.meaning: Wind direction on the ground plane; normalized.

options.name: strength
options.meaning: Largest sideways tip offset of the sway.

options.name: spatialFrequency
options.meaning: How fast the sway's phase changes along the wind, so waves travel across a field.

options.name: gustStrength
options.meaning: Gusts add up to this fraction of strength, always downwind.

options.name: height
options.meaning: Blade height in the geometry: y = 0 is the root, y = height the tip.

options.name: stiffness
options.meaning: Exponent of the height weighting; higher keeps the lower blade straighter.

options.name: lightDirection
options.meaning: Direction toward the light for the simple two-sided shading.

limits: Stylized, not a physical simulation: no blade collision, no recovery dynamics, and the bend is a shear of each vertex, not a rotation, so strong wind stretches blades slightly (the drop keeps the length only to first order). Shading is a simple two-sided term with one light direction; three.js lights, shadows and fog are ignored. Geometry must stand on y = 0 with its tip at y = height in object space; instance scale stretches the blade but the wind offset is in world units. Normals are not bent with the blade. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Travelling layered sine waves along the wind direction
1D value noise on PCG-style integer hashes for gusts
Second-order length-preserving drop of a sheared tip
